summary: Players slide bamboo/incense tokens into grooved home boards to pick actions across four rounds of four seasons, placing tiles to build a balanced (left/right symmetric) farm while burning incense at shared temples for spirit bonuses. It plays as a relaxed, puzzly tile-optimization game rather than a tense strategy title — reviewers describe it as cozy and contemplative.
praised: The tactile bamboo/incense sliding action-selection mechanism, called unique and satisfying
Artwork and overall thematic mood (whimsical, gorgeous)
Depth in the home-tile placement puzzle from the balance requirement
criticised: Iconography and UI problems: key tile info tucked in small corners, tiny alignment arrows, oversized trackers wasting board space
Summed up by one reviewer as 'everyone likes it, no one loves it' — solidly good but rarely a favorite
Minor component complaints (excess currency tokens, tile holders that spill)

interaction.kind: drafting limited action spots shared by all players
interaction.detail: Players take turns claiming action spaces that become unavailable to others that round, but the deeper game — arranging bamboo tiles and family needs — plays out on each player's own board. The shared element is mainly about action-order timing rather than players actively targeting one another's positions.
interaction.said: unknown — I don't have confident recall of recurring player commentary on this title's interactivity

sources: happiness points for meeting family needs
scoring.how_you_win: Over four years split into four seasonal phases, cultivate bamboo and use it to satisfy family needs and temple offerings for happiness points; after the fixed number of rounds, the player with the most happiness points wins.
